desc: Implement a function to compute `Ways(A, B, k)`: number of ways to choose $k$ edges between sets of size $A$ and $B$ such that every node in $B$ has at least one edge. This can be done using inclusion-exclusion: $\sum_{j=0}^B (-1)^j \binom{B}{j} \binom{A(B-j)}{k}$.

Generate all valid layerings. A layering is defined by the sequence of sizes $s_1, s_2, \dots, s_D$ such that $\sum s_i = N-1$ and $\sum_{i \text{ even}} s_i = N/2 - 1$ (since $s_0=1$ is even, we need $N/2 - 1$ more even-layer vertices).
For each valid layering, construct the polynomial for edge counts.
Inter-layer terms: $P_{inter}(x) = \prod_{i=1}^D (\sum_k Ways(s_{i-1}, s_i, k) x^k)$.
Sum the coefficients of $x^M$ from all valid layerings' polynomials.
